title: Gluing local immersions representing a source-local predicate
statement: Let $S$ be a scheme [def-pc-scheme]. For each morphism $g:T\to S$ let $P(g)$ be a proposition. Suppose $P(g)$ implies $P(g\circ h)$ for every $h:T'\to T$, and suppose $P(g)$ holds whenever every point of $T$ has an open neighbourhood $V$ with $P(g\circ\iota_V)$. Assume that for each $s\in S$ there exist an open neighbourhood $U$, a scheme $W_U$, and an immersion $j_U:W_U\to U$ representing the predicate: for all $g:T\to U$, $g$ factors through $j_U$ if and only if $P(\iota_U\circ g)$. Then there exist a scheme $W$ and an immersion $j:W\to S$ with, for all $g:T\to S$, $g$ factors through $j$ if and only if $P(g)$.

proof.text: Choose U, W_i and j_i from hlocal. For maps a into U_i and b into U_k with equal composites to S, rewrite both factorization propositions using the local representing criteria. They become the same proposition P, so compatibility holds. Apply lem-sc-compatible-immersion-gluing to obtain Z, q and the Cartesian charts.

Form the open cover of S indexed by its points using the chosen U_i. The chart Cartesian squares identify the pullback of q over U_i with j_i. Transport IsImmersion across this isomorphism and use target locality to deduce IsImmersion q. The universal property of each Cartesian square identifies factors of a: T to U_i through j_i with factors of a followed by U_i inclusion through q. These steps are written in Lean using IsZariskiLocalAtTarget.of_openCover and IsPullback.lift.

For P(g), at each t in T use U_(g(t)) and its inverse image V in T. Base-change stability gives P(V inclusion followed by g). The local criterion and the Cartesian square give a factor through q on V. Since an immersion is a monomorphism, these factors agree on overlaps by cancelling q. Scheme.Cover.glueMorphisms gives a global factor, and Scheme.Cover.hom_ext checks its composite equals g. This also handles empty T: the empty open cover glues the empty family of maps.

Conversely suppose g factors through q. Restrict this factor to V, the inverse image of U_(g(t)), for each t. The Cartesian chart criterion and the local representing criterion give P on V. Apply hsource to obtain P(g). For empty S the geometric lemma allows the empty gluing, and every source-locality argument has a vacuous pointwise hypothesis when T is empty.
